title: Pictograms, Tally Charts and Bar Charts
seo_title: Pictograms – Primary 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Collect data and make pictograms; read pictograms, tally charts and bar charts; answer questions from data. (summary of the NERDC Primary 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 maths worksheets on data: reading pictograms with a key, tally charts, block graphs and bar charts, and comparing data. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: One picture may stand for more than one thing.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A pictogram uses pictures to show data. The key tells how many each picture stands for.
  • A tally chart uses marks: |||| with a line across is 5.
  • To compare, find the difference between two amounts.

Examples

Example

Key: 1 picture = 2 pupils. Mangoes has 4 pictures

4 × 2

Answer: 8 pupils

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Ignoring the keyMultiply by what one picture stands for.
Miscounting tally marksCount the groups of 5 first.
Adding when asked how many moreSubtract to compare.

faq.q: What does a tally mark show?

faq.a: So one picture can stand for several things.

items.q: How many blackbirds were seen?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 2 birds. The Blackbird row has 5 circles: 5 × 2 = 10 birds.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 lollies. The Lemon row has 1 star: 1 × 5 = 5 lollies.

items.q: How many pupils come by bus to school?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 10 pupils. The Bus row has 5 squares and half a square: 5 × 10 = 50, and half of 10 is 5, so 50 + 5 = 55 pupils.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a circle stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole circle = 10 cakes. Half a circle is half of 10, which is 5 cakes, not 1.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 shells. The Ngozi row has 6 stars: 6 × 5 = 30 shells.

items.q: Which row shows the most votes?
items.e: Every square stands for the same number, so the row with the most squares shows the most. The Banana row has 5 squares: 5 × 2 = 10 votes.

items.q: Each star stands for 2 books. Uju read 9 books. How many stars should be in her row?
items.e: Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. 4 whole stars make 8. 1 more is half of 2, so add half a star. Draw 4 and a half stars.
Look at the key: each star stands for 2 stickers. The Zainab row has 3 stars and half a star: 3 × 2 = 6, and half of 2 is 1, so 6 + 1 = 7 stickers.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a square stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole square = 10 votes. Half a square is half of 10, which is 5 votes, not 1.

items.q: Which row shows 11 books?
items.e: Half a circle is 1, so 11 books is 5 and a half circles. The Uju row has 5 circles and half a circle: 5 × 2 = 10, and half of 2 is 1, so 10 + 1 = 11 books.
Look at the key: each star stands for 10 cans. The 3B row has 4 stars and half a star: 4 × 10 = 40, and half of 10 is 5, so 40 + 5 = 45 cans.

items.q: Which row shows the fewest pupils?
items.e: Every square stands for the same number, so the row with the fewest squares shows the fewest. The Rugby row has 1 square: 1 × 5 = 5 pupils.

items.q: Each circle stands for 10 pupils. 45 pupils walk to school. How many circles should be in the Walk row?
items.e: Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. 4 whole circles make 40. 5 more is half of 10, so add half a circle. Draw 4 and a half circles.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 books. The Animals row has 6 stars: 6 × 5 = 30 books.

items.q: How many pupils have a rabbit?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 2 pupils. The Rabbit row has 1 square and half a square: 1 × 2 = 2, and half of 2 is 1, so 2 + 1 = 3 pupils.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a circle stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole circle = 10 points. Half a circle is half of 10, which is 5 points, not 1.
Half a star is 5, so 25 pupils is 2 and a half stars. The Bike row has 2 stars and half a star: 2 × 10 = 20, and half of 10 is 5, so 20 + 5 = 25 pupils.

items.q: How many spiders were found?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 5 minibeasts. The Spider row has 2 squares: 2 × 5 = 10 minibeasts.

items.q: Each square stands for 5 votes. Red got 30 votes. How many squares should be in the Red row?
items.e: Count in 5s until you reach 30: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 squares. Check: 6 × 5 = 30.
Look at the key: each star stands for 10 lollies. The Orange row has 1 star and half a star: 1 × 10 = 10, and half of 10 is 5, so 10 + 5 = 15 lollies.

items.q: How many blue tits were seen?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 2 birds, so half a circle = 1. The Blue tit row has 7 circles. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. So it is 14 blue tits.
Look at the key: each star = 5 children. The Vanilla row has 5 stars. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. So it is 25 children.

items.q: How many children chose oranges?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Orange row has 3 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. So it is 30 children.

items.q: How many woodlice were found?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 2 minibeasts, so half a circle = 1. The Woodlouse row has 2 circles. Count in 2s: 2, 4. So it is 4 woodlice.
Look at the key: each star = 2 children, so half a star = 1. The Hamster row has 1 star and half a star. Count in 2s: 2, then 1 more for the half. So it is 3 children.
Look at the key: each star = 5 children. The Skipping row has 4 stars. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. So it is 20 children.

items.q: How many children chose green?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Green row has 8 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80. So it is 80 children.
Look at the key: each star = 2 cars, so half a star = 1. The Blue row has 4 stars and half a star. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, then 1 more for the half. So it is 9 cars.

items.q: Each square stands for 5 children. 20 children chose tag. How many squares go in the Tag row?
items.e: Count in 5s until you reach 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 steps, so draw 4 squares, not 20.

items.q: Each circle stands for 10 children. 60 children walk to school. How many circles go in the Walk row?
items.e: Count in 10s until you reach 60: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 circles, not 60.

items.q: How many children walk to school?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Walk row has 5 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. So it is 50 children.

items.q: How many children chose tag?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 2 children, so half a square = 1. The Tag row has 6 squares and half a square. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, then 1 more for the half. So it is 13 children.

items.q: Which fruit is the most popular?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 5 children. The Pear row has the most circles: 6 circles. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. So it is 30 children.

items.q: Each star stands for 2 children. 7 children chose mint. What goes in the Mint row?
items.e: Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6. That is 3 stars, which makes 6. 1 more is half of 2, so add half a star. Draw 3 and a half stars.

items.q: Which colour is the least popular?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Purple row has the fewest squares: 2 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20. So it is 20 children.
Look at the key: each heart = 5 children. Vanilla: 5 hearts = 25. Mint: 3 hearts = 15. How many more means subtract: 25 − 15 = 10.

items.q: How many more children come by bike than come by bus?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 10 children. Bike: 5 circles = 50. Bus: 2 circles = 20. How many more means subtract: 50 − 20 = 30.

items.q: How many children have a hamster or a cat?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 2 children, so half a square = 1. Hamster: 15. Cat: 7. Altogether means add: 15 + 7 = 22.

items.q: How many children come by bike or come by bus?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. Bike: 60. Bus: 20. Altogether means add: 60 + 20 = 80.
Look at the key: each heart = 5 children. Tag: 6 hearts = 30. Football: 4 hearts = 20. How many fewer means subtract: 30 − 20 = 10.

items.q: How many black cars were there?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Black row has 3 groups of 5 and 4 more: 3 × 5 = 15, and 15 + 4 = 19.

items.q: How many red cars were there?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Red row has 2 groups of 5 and 4 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 4 = 14.

items.q: How many votes did Apple get?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Apple row has 3 groups of 5 and 4 more: 3 × 5 = 15, and 15 + 4 = 19.

items.q: Which row shows 6 votes?
items.e: 6 = 5 + 1. Look for 1 group of 5 and 1 single mark. That is the Banana row.

items.q: How many lorries went past the school?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Lorry row has 2 groups of 5 and 4 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 4 = 14.

items.q: How many vehicles are shown in the tally chart altogether?
items.e: Count each row: Car 18, Van 3, Lorry 14, Bus 7. Then add: 18 + 3 + 14 + 7 = 42 vehicles.

items.q: How many snails were found?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Snail row has 2 groups of 5 and 1 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 1 = 11.

items.q: What is the difference between the biggest and the smallest number of minibeasts?
items.e: The biggest is Spider (18). The smallest is Worm (9). Difference means subtract: 18 − 9 = 9.

items.q: Which row shows 17 pupils?
items.e: 17 = 5 + 5 + 5 + 2. Look for 3 groups of 5 and 2 single marks. That is the Netball row.

items.q: How many pupils are shown in the tally chart altogether?
items.e: Count each row: Football 12, Netball 17, Swimming 18, Cricket 8. Then add: 12 + 17 + 18 + 8 = 55 pupils.

items.q: How many snails did class 3A find?
items.e: Find the Snails row, then go across to the Class 3A column. The cell says 17.

items.q: How many worms did the two classes find altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the two cells in the Worms row: 3 + 12 = 15.

items.q: How many more spiders did class 3A find than class 3B?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: 11 − 5 = 6.

items.q: Which minibeast did the two classes find the most of altogether?
items.e: Add each row: Ladybirds 15 + 8 = 23, Worms 3 + 12 = 15, Snails 17 + 4 = 21, Spiders 11 + 5 = 16. The biggest total is 23, for ladybirds.

items.q: How many books did Funke read in week 2?
items.e: Find the Funke row, then go across to the Week 2 column. The cell says 13.

items.q: How many books did the four pupils read in week 2?
items.e: Add the whole Week 2 column: 3 + 13 + 5 + 12 = 33.

items.q: How many more books did Kelechi read in week 1 than in week 2?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: 7 − 3 = 4.

items.q: How many pupils had a hot dinner on Wednesday?
items.e: Find the Wednesday row, then go across to the Hot dinner column. The cell says 16.

items.q: How many pupils had lunch on Tuesday altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the two cells in the Tuesday row: 9 + 21 = 30.

items.q: How many pupils had a hot dinner from Monday to Thursday?
items.e: Add the whole Hot dinner column: 13 + 9 + 16 + 8 = 46.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 2s.

items.q: How many shells did Amaka find?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Amaka bar ends on the line for 2. So the answer is 2 shells.

items.q: How many pupils come by bus to school?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Bus bar ends on the line for 20. So the answer is 20 pupils.

items.q: How many cans did class 3D collect?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The 3D bar ends halfway between 50 and 60, so it shows 55. So the answer is 55 cans.

items.q: How many woodlice were found?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Woodlouse bar ends on the line for 8. So the answer is 8 minibeasts.

items.q: Which bar shows 15 books?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Find 15 on the scale. The Animals bar ends on the line for 15.

items.q: How many points did Falcon House get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Falcon bar ends halfway between 30 and 40, so it shows 35. So the answer is 35 points.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 5, 10, 15 … Each line is 5 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 5s.

items.q: Which bar shows the most birds?
items.e: The Sparrow bar is the tallest one. The Sparrow bar ends on the line for 14. It shows 14 birds.

items.q: How many votes did Green get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Green bar ends halfway between 60 and 70, so it shows 65. So the answer is 65 votes.

items.q: How many lemon lollies were sold?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Lemon bar ends on the line for 25. So the answer is 25 lollies.

items.q: How many pupils chose swimming?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Swimming bar ends halfway between 8 and 10, so it shows 9. So the answer is 9 pupils.

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest votes?
items.e: The Apple bar is the shortest one. The Apple bar ends on the line for 10. It shows 10 votes.

items.q: How many stickers has Kayode got?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Kayode bar ends on the line for 25. So the answer is 25 stickers.

items.q: How many pupils have a cat?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Cat bar ends halfway between 4 and 6, so it shows 5. So the answer is 5 pupils.

items.q: Which bar shows 55 cakes?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Find 55 on the scale. The Wed bar ends halfway between 50 and 60, so it shows 55.

items.q: How many points did Owl House get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Owl bar ends on the line for 30. So the answer is 30 points.

items.q: Which bar shows the most books?
items.e: The Space bar is the tallest one. The Space bar ends on the line for 30. It shows 30 books.

items.q: How many shells did Femi find?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Femi bar ends halfway between 12 and 14, so it shows 13. So the answer is 13 shells.

items.q: Which bar shows 2 pupils?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Find 2 on the scale. The Rugby bar ends on the line for 2.

items.q: How many more shells did Ngozi find than Amaka?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Ngozi 11 and Amaka 3. How many more means find the difference: 11 − 3 = 8 shells.
Each star = 5. Space 5 × 5 = 25 and Sport 3 × 5 = 15. Altogether means add: 25 + 15 = 40 books.

items.q: How many fewer votes did Orange get than Pear?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Pear 50 and Orange 40. How many fewer means find the difference: 50 − 40 = 10 votes.

items.q: How many more books did Kelechi read than Yusuf?
items.e: Each circle = 2, so half a circle = 1. Kelechi 3 × 2 = 6 and Yusuf 1 × 2 = 2. How many more means find the difference: 6 − 2 = 4 books.

items.q: How many blue tits and robins were seen altogether?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Blue tit 20 and Robin 15. Altogether means add: 20 + 15 = 35 birds.

items.q: How many fewer points did Kestrel House get than Falcon House?
items.e: Each square = 10, so half a square = 5. Falcon 3 × 10 = 30 and Kestrel 2 × 10 = 20. How many fewer means find the difference: 30 − 20 = 10 points.

items.q: How many stickers have they got altogether?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Read every bar: Zainab 11, Kayode 10, Joy 3, Mohammed 4. Add them: 11 + 10 + 3 + 4 = 28 stickers.

items.q: How many more cans did class 3A collect than 3B?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. 3A 25 and 3B 20. How many more means find the difference: 25 − 20 = 5 cans.

items.q: How many votes did Red and Purple get altogether?
items.e: Each square = 10, so half a square = 5. Red 2 × 10 = 20 and Purple 5 × 10 = 50. Altogether means add: 20 + 50 = 70 votes.

items.q: How many fewer pupils have a fish than a hamster?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Hamster 12 and Fish 7. How many fewer means find the difference: 12 − 7 = 5 pupils.

items.q: How many more cakes were sold on Tuesday than on Monday and Thursday together?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Tue 25, Mon 5 and Thu 10. Step 1: Monday and Thursday together: 5 + 10 = 15. Step 2: 25 − 15 = 10 cakes.

items.q: How many pupils are in the survey altogether?
items.e: Each square = 5. Read every row: Walk 5 × 5 = 25, Bike 4 × 5 = 20, Bus 6 × 5 = 30, Car 3 × 5 = 15. Add them: 25 + 20 + 30 + 15 = 90 pupils.

items.q: How many more pupils chose swimming than cricket?
items.e: Each circle = 10, so half a circle = 5. Swimming 6 × 10 = 60 and Cricket 4 × 10 = 40. How many more means find the difference: 60 − 40 = 20 pupils.
Each star = 2, so half a star = 1. Ladybird 3 × 2 + 1 = 7, Woodlouse 2 × 2 + 1 = 5 and Spider 3 × 2 = 6. Step 1: woodlice and spiders together: 5 + 6 = 11. Step 2: 11 − 7 = 4 minibeasts fewer.

items.q: Primary 3 want to collect 150 cans altogether. How many more cans do they need?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Step 1: read every bar and add: 10 + 30 + 20 + 40 = 100. Step 2: 150 − 100 = 50 cans.

items.q: How many more votes did Yellow get than Purple and Blue together?
items.e: Each circle = 10, so half a circle = 5. Yellow 6 × 10 = 60, Purple 1 × 10 = 10 and Blue 3 × 10 = 30. Step 1: Purple and Blue together: 10 + 30 = 40. Step 2: 60 − 40 = 20 votes.
Each star = 5. Lemon 6 × 5 = 30 and Cherry 3 × 5 = 15. How many fewer means find the difference: 30 − 15 = 15 lollies.

items.q: How many fewer cakes were sold on Friday than on Thursday and Wednesday together?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Fri 50, Thu 20 and Wed 40. Step 1: Thursday and Wednesday together: 20 + 40 = 60. Step 2: 60 − 50 = 10 cakes fewer.

items.q: The pupils want to read 100 books altogether this term. How many more books must they read?
items.e: Each circle = 5. Step 1: read every row and add: 10 + 30 + 15 + 5 = 60. Step 2: 100 − 60 = 40 books.

items.q: How many more shells did Victor find than Ngozi and Amaka together?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Victor 10, Ngozi 2 and Amaka 4. Step 1: Ngozi and Amaka together: 2 + 4 = 6. Step 2: 10 − 6 = 4 shells.
